Rashi on Shabbat 134a:10:2.hebrew: מאי שנא מלישה - שלשין פת ביום טוב, והאי נמי ללישה דמיא:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:10:2.english: In what [way] is [it] different from kneading - For they knead bread on a Festival, and this too resembles kneading.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:10:3.hebrew: לא אפשר - דפת חמה מעליא טפי. הכא אפשר מאתמול:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:10:3.english: It is not possible - For warm bread is much better; here, it is possible [to do so] from yesterday.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:11:1.hebrew: אימא אף גבינתא בת יומא מעליא - וכ"ש דאתמול:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:11:1.english: Say: Even one-day-old cheese is excellent - And all the more so [cheese] from yesterday.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:12:1.hebrew: לפניה לסטריה לעילאי - לאימרא שבשפת פיה יהפוך ויקפל למעלה, שלא תהא סמוכה לבשרו, מפני שראש מקום חתך הבגד שם הוא, ויוצאין ממנו גרדין שקורין פיינד"ץ (ציציות). ודלמא מדביקא גרדתא מיניה במכה, וכשבא להפשיט החלוק מעל המילה, ישמוט ויקרע את ראש הגיד ומשוי ליה כרות שפכה:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:12:1.english: Turn its edge upward - The hem at the edge of its opening he should turn and fold upward, so that it will not be next to his flesh, because the edge of the cut part of the garment is there, and threads protrude from it, which are called peindz (fringes). And [there is concern] lest a thread from it stick to the wound, and when one comes to remove the pouch from over the circumcision, it will pull and tear the tip of the member and render him [one with] a severed urethra.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:12:3.english: She would make [it] - For the babies who came into her care to tend to their circumcision.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:12:4.hebrew: כיסתתא לפלגא - דמילה. כיס היתה עושה של בגד לפנים בתוך החלוק, ותופרתו מתוכו בתוך החלוק, ומגיע למטה עד חצי החלוק, כדי לחוץ בין האימרא ובין המילה:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:12:4.english: A pouch for half - [of] the circumcision. She would make a pouch of cloth inside, within the garment, and sew it from the inside, within the garment, and it would reach downward to half of the garment, in order to interpose between the hem and the circumcision.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:12:5.hebrew: לייתי בליתא - מעט שחק של בגד שיהא בו אימרא, לפי שהאימרא מהדקה יפה בבשר, שלא ישמט החלוק מן הגיד:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:12:5.english: Let one bring a worn-out rag - [That is,] a small piece of a worn-out garment that has a hem, because the hem grips well onto the flesh so that the pouch will not slip off the organ.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:12:6.hebrew: וליפכיה לשפתיה לתתאי - לתחתית ראש הגיד יתן השפה, וראש השני החלק יהא למעלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:12:6.english: And let him turn its hem downward - At the bottom of the tip of the member he should place the hem, and the other, smooth end should be on top.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:12:7.hebrew: ולעפיה לעילאי - אותו ראש העליון החלוק יקפל ויקפול כלפי חוץ, מפני הגרדין שלא ידבקו במכה:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:12:7.english: And let him fold it upward - That upper end [of] the pouch he should fold over and over toward the outside, because of the threads, so that they do not stick to the wound.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:1.english: Whose exit is not known in him - [Meaning] that the opening of the rectum is not discernible in him, where his excrement exits.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:10.english: And let one stand it opposite his mouth - And he should stand [it] near his mouth.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:11.english: So that his mouth will warm - That his mouth will become warm.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:12.english: And he will nurse - And he will suckle.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:13.hebrew: דלא מינשתא - שאין נשימה ניכרת בו, שאין דופק כנגד לבו כדרך כל אדם:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:13.english: That does not breathe - [Meaning] that breathing is not discernible in him, [and] that there is no pulse opposite his heart in the manner of every person.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:14.english: Let one fan him with a sieve - They should fan over him with a sieve that is called "van" [in Old French].

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:2.english: Let one rub it with oil - For the oil makes the flesh shine.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:3.english: And let one stand him before the day - Opposite the sun.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:4.hebrew: והיכא דזיג - שצלול כזכוכית, בידוע שהחלל כנגדו:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:4.english: And where it is transparent - [Where] it is clear like glass, it is known that the cavity is opposite it.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:5.english: With a barley grain - With the tip of the barley grain, which is sharp.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:6.hebrew: דזריף - מנפחו, אינפליי"ר בלע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:6.english: Because it causes swelling - It causes it to swell; enfler in Old French.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:7.english: Who does not suck - [Meaning] that he is unable to nurse.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:8.english: It is [that] his mouth has grown cold - His lips have become chilled, and he has no strength to suck with them.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:13:9.english: They should bring a cup of coals - She should spread coals on a board or on a vessel.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:14:1.hebrew: דלא מעוי - אין רוחו נכנס ויוצא יפה, אליינ"א בלע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:14:1.english: That does not breathe - His breath does not enter and exit well, aleine [breath] in Old French.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:14:10.hebrew: לא נפל ביה דמא - לא בא בו דם, ומתוך כך חלש הוא ואין בו כח, וממהר לחלוש ולמות:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:14:10.english: His blood has not fallen into him - Blood has not come into him, and because of this he is weak and has no strength, and is quick to grow weak and die.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:14:2.english: His mother's placenta - [The] afterbirth that was born with him.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:14:3.hebrew: ולישרקיה עליה - יחליקנה על בשרו, כמו אישתרוקי אישתריקו (ע"ג ד' מ:), אשאולדי"ר:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:14:3.english: And let him smooth it over him - He should smooth it over his flesh, like [the expression] ishtarrukei ishtarriku ("[they] slipped," Avodah Zarah 40b), [meaning] "to slide" [in Old French].

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:14:4.english: Who is small - [Meaning] that he is thin.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:14:5.hebrew: מקוטנא לאולמא - השליא ראשה א' קצר וראשה אחד רחב. יחליקוה עליו: מראש הקצר יתחילו וימשוכו לצד הרחב, כלומר: כן ירחיב זה ויתעבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:14:5.english: From the narrow [end] to the wide [end] - The placenta has one narrow end and one wide end. They should rub it over him: they should begin from the narrow end and draw [it] toward the wide side, that is to say, thus will this [child] widen and thicken.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:14:6.hebrew: ואי אלים - ולא מחמת בריאות אלא נפוח, לישרקיה עליה מאולמא לקוטנא:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:14:6.english: And if [the baby] is large - [That is,] not out of health, but rather swollen — let them stroke [it] over him from the wide [end] to the narrow [end].

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:14:7.english: That is red - All his flesh is red.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:14:8.hebrew: לא איבלע ביה דמיה - בבשרו, דעכשיו כל דמו מצוי בין עור לבשר, וכשמוהלין אותו יוצא כל דמו:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:14:8.english: His blood has not been absorbed in him - [In] his flesh, for now all his blood is present between skin and flesh, and when they circumcise him, all his blood flows out.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:14:9.english: Let them wait for him - They should wait [before] circumcising him.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:15:1.hebrew: לכרכי הים - ה"ג: ראיתיו שהיה ירוק, הצצתי בו ולא היה בו דם ברית. תרתי לגריעותא: חדא, דאי מהיל ליה לא נפק מיניה דמא, והטפת דם ברית מצוה, כדכתיב (זכריה ט׳:י״א) גם את בדם בריתך. ועוד, דמסוכן הוא, ומשום חולשא שלא נוצר בו עדיין דם:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:15:1.english: To the coastal cities - This is the reading: "I saw that he was green [pale]; I looked at him and there was no blood of the covenant in him." [There are] two drawbacks: First, if one circumcises him, no blood will come out of him, whereas drawing a drop of the blood of the covenant is a mitzvah, as it is written (Zechariah 9:11), "As for you also, because of the blood of your covenant." And furthermore, he is in danger, and [this is] due to weakness, as blood has not yet formed in him.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:1:1.hebrew: חספניתא - פניו מתבקעות. ואני אומר שהוא מין שחין שקורין אינייר"א, והוא (בגרב) ובחרס שכתוב בתורה (דברים כח), וחספניתא תרגום של חרס:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:1:1.english: Chaspanita - His face cracks. And I say that it is a type of skin eruption called "einiere" [in Old French], and it is "(with a scab) and with an itch [cheres]" that is written in the Torah (Deuteronomy 28[:27]), for "chaspanita" is the Targum [Aramaic translation] of "cheres".

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:3:1.english: Suitable for a sick person - Who is not in [life-threatening] danger.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:4:1.english: [Will your words] be negated - For this [person] too is a sick person.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:4:2.hebrew: אבל לכולי עלמא שרי - לדעת ר"מ, וסתם מתני' ר"מ היא, ואמאי תנן "נותן זה בעצמו וזה בעצמו":
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:4:2.english: But for everyone it is permitted - [According to] Rabbi Meir, and an unattributed Mishnah [follows] Rabbi Meir; so why did [the Mishnah] teach: "He puts this one by itself and that one by itself"?

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:5:2.english: They do not need beating - [That is,] to beat it and mix it thoroughly.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:5:3.english: But not beat [it] - He should not mix it so much.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:5:4.english: And [the Gemara] answers: That is what [the Mishnah] teaches: he places this by itself and that by itself - [meaning] that he mixes [them] and does not beat [them].

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:6:1.hebrew: אין מסננין את החרדל - בי"ט:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:6:1.english: One may not strain mustard - On a Festival.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:6:2.hebrew: במסננת שלו - טעמא מפרש לקמיה, דמיחזי כבורר שמשליך הסובין שלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:6:2.english: In its strainer - The reason is explained further on, for it appears like selecting, since one discards its bran.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:6:3.english: And one may not sweeten it with a coal - In the manner that they are accustomed to extinguish a coal or a heated stone in it.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:6:4.english: One may place an egg in a mustard strainer - And [one] strains it inside it to beautify its appearance.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:7:1.english: It does not appear like selecting - For all of it [the egg] passes through the strainer, and no refuse remains there.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:8:1.hebrew: בגחלת של עץ - אסור, דשייך בה כיבוי, לפי שעושה פחם. גחלת של מתכת, לא שייך בה כיבוי, דאינו נעשה פחם:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:8:1.english: With a wooden coal - [It is] prohibited, as [the prohibition of] extinguishing applies to it, since it makes charcoal. [With] a metal coal, [the prohibition of] extinguishing does not apply to it, as it does not become charcoal.

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:9:1.hebrew: ומ"ש מבישרא אגומרי - שצולין בי"ט, ואע"ג דמכבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:9:1.english: And how is it different from meat on coals - That we roast on a Festival, even though it extinguishes [the coals].

Rashi on Shabbat 134a:9:2.hebrew: לא אפשר - לצלות מאתמול, דביומא שביחא טפי; אבל חרדל אפשר מאתמול:
Rashi on Shabbat 134a:9:2.english: It is not possible - to roast [the meat] from yesterday [i.e., before Shabbat], for on the [same] day it is better; however, mustard is possible [to prepare] from yesterday.

Tosafot on Shabbat 134a:7:1.hebrew: הכא מיחזי כבורר - מיהו בורר לא הוי, שגם הפסולת ראוי לאכילה, ולא דמי למשמרת דריש תולין (לקמן שבת ד' קלז:), דאיכא למ"ד חייב משום בורר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 134a:7:1.english: Here it appears like selecting - However, it is not [actually] selecting, since even the refuse is fit for eating, and it is not comparable to [the case of] the strainer at the beginning of [the chapter] Tolin (below, Shabbat 137b), where there is an opinion that says one is liable on account of selecting.
